name: Muslim Community Network
mission: Muslim Community Network is dedicated to redefining and shaping the Muslim experience in the United States through community education, leadership development and advocacy.

geographicCoverage: New York City (New York, United States)
Brooklyn (Kings County, New York, United States)

theoryOfChange: Muslim Community Network envisions a future where the Muslim community, rich in its diverse and intersecting identities, stands united in championing peace, justice, and inclusivity. Our vision extends beyond intra-community harmony to encompass collaborative engagement with a mosaic of other communities, fostering a society where mutual understanding and respect are the norm. This ambitious vision is anchored in our unwavering commitment to three core pillars: Community Education, Leadership Development and Advocacy.

strengths_deep_dive: The Muslim Community Network balances programmatic reach with stable administrative management. By maintaining an <cite id="1">80.1% program expense ratio</cite>, the organization ensures most donor funds directly support community training and youth programs. This financial efficiency is paired with a <cite id="4">93.8 Accountability rating from Charity Navigator</cite>, showing clear internal financial controls.
rich_narrative.summary: The Muslim Community Network uses civic education and youth leadership development to shape the public narrative around American Muslims <cite id="1">since its founding in 2003</cite>. Operating primarily across New York City, the organization runs programs like the Impact Academy, youth empowerment initiatives, and community support services <cite id="1">with total revenue reaching $1,153,075</cite>. In FY2025, financial filings show the charity directed <cite id="1">80.1% of its expenses to program operations</cite>. The organization holds a <cite id="4">Charity Navigator score of 87.0/100</cite> and receives awards from local government bodies, including the New York City Council. While program execution and financial health remain balanced, small board oversight and executive pay relative to revenue represent key areas for structural growth.
